capabilities: Render GLB, glTF, STL, OBJ, PLY and other 3D files in a pane or as wiki embeds
Orbit, zoom and pan models and save camera angles into code blocks
Move and scale top-level nodes of glTF/GLB models in an edit mode
Describe models as text with the shapes code block or generate them from LLM prompts
Show gcode printer paths and xyz/pcd files as lines or point clouds
extras: Draco-compressed glTF files cannot be read (Meshopt works); mobile works but large models are slow and the browser caps simultaneous WebGL contexts. Model-by-prompt sends prompts to Anthropic when a Claude entry is used.
intentEvidence: 3D files behave like PDFs: click to open, ![[…]] to embed.
motivation: The README states that generated 3D output usually lives next to the note discussing it, but you have to leave Obsidian to look at it; the plugin keeps it in place.
problem: Generated 3D output (CAD exports, scans, floor plans) sits next to notes but Obsidian cannot display it, so users must leave the app to view it.

relations.evidence: src/viewer/ wraps three.js and knows nothing about Obsidian.
or a Claude entry of the LLM Endpoint Manager

summary: 3D model viewer that renders GLB, glTF, STL and other 3D files inline in notes, with orbit/zoom/pan controls and a limited node editor.
